title: VII. Living OT specimens; Sadducee origin from Antigonus — Cap. 10 close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Twisting such that sentence worse, they inferred no reward belonging toward good deeds, no hope belonging toward another life — to ye which Paul alluded in Acts 23:6. he commanded not so much by hope belonging toward reward as out from love. The occasion belonging toward erring stood as taken by Sadoc out from Antigonus belonging toward Socho's words: Be not like servants who serve ye Lord to receive a portion; One wonders such that ye Sadducees so obstinately denied it. || 2 Kings 4:35 plus 13:21. The splendid plus living specimens by ye which under ye OT ye resurrection belonging toward ye dead stands as established stand as God's wondrous works recalling some out from death to life: ye widow belonging toward Sarepta's son by Elijah, ye Shunammite's son by Elisha, plus ye man who revived at Elisha's bones — 1 Kings 17:22; VII.
pass_b_english: VII. The splendid and living specimens by which under the OT the resurrection of the dead is established are God's wondrous works recalling some from death to life: the widow of Sarepta's son by Elijah, the Shunammite's son by Elisha, and the man who revived at Elisha's bones — 1 Kings 17:22; 2 Kings 4:35 and 13:21.

One wonders that the Sadducees so obstinately denied it. The occasion of erring was taken by Sadoc from Antigonus of Socho's words: Be not like servants who serve the Lord to receive a portion; he commanded not so much by hope of reward as from love. Twisting that sentence worse, they inferred no reward of good deeds, no hope of another life — to which Paul alluded in Acts 23:6.
source_text: VII. Luculenta & viva specimina, quibus sub V.T. resurrectio mortuorum adstruitur, sunt miranda Dei opera, quibus nonnulli e morte in vitam sunt revocati. Huc pertinent filius viduae Sareptanae ab Elia, filius Sunamitidis ab Elisaeo, & vir contactis Elisaei ossibus reviviscens, 1 Reg. 17.22; 2 Reg. 4.35 & 13.21. Mirari subit quod Sadducaei tam obstinate negaverint. Occasio errandi a Sadoco e verbis Antigoni Sochaei: ne sitis tanquam servi qui ideo Domino serviunt ut demensum accipiant; jubebat non tam spe mercedis quam ex amore. Quam sententiam in deteriorem partem rapientes inferebant nullam esse benefactorum mercedem, nullam spem alterius vitae: quorsum allusit Paulus Act. 23.v.6.
